checks.label: AppOps: private-data access
checks.description: Apps with access to external storage or fine location - evidence collector, review for suspicious entries.
checks.remediation: Revoke permissions for suspicious apps: appops set <package> <op> ignore

checks.label: Security Tools Detected
checks.description: Pentest frameworks or hacking tools found
checks.remediation: Uninstall detected pentest tools: pm uninstall <package>

checks.label: Apps Installed Last 7 Days
checks.command: current=$(date +%s); for pkg in $(pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2 | head -15); do ft=$(dumpsys package $pkg 2>/dev/null | grep firstInstallTime | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$ft" ] && d=$(( (current - ft/1000) / 86400 )) && [ $d -lt 7 ] && echo "$pkg (${d}d)"; done
checks.description: Third-party apps installed in last 7 days - review for legitimacy
checks.remediation: Review each recently installed app and uninstall any unauthorized ones: pm uninstall <package>

checks.label: Apps Not From Play Store
checks.command: pm list packages -3 -i 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'installer=com.android.vending' | grep -v 'installer=com.google' | head -10
checks.description: Apps installed from non-Play Store sources - higher malware risk
checks.remediation: Uninstall sideloaded apps: pm uninstall <package>. Disable unknown sources to prevent future installs.

checks.label: APK Signature Path Check
checks.description: Checks for valid APK path info
checks.remediation: If no valid APK path is returned, verify package integrity with: pm verify <package>

checks.label: Suspicious APK Names
checks.remediation: Uninstall suspicious packages immediately: pm uninstall <package>

checks.label: Debuggable Apps (Strict)
checks.command: for pkg in $(pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2 | head -20); do dumpsys package $pkg 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'DEBUGGABLE' && echo $pkg; done
checks.description: Third-party apps with debuggable flag enabled
checks.remediation: Uninstall debuggable apps: pm uninstall <package>. Replace with release (non-debug) builds.

checks.label: APK Signature Verification
checks.remediation: Enable package verification: settings put global package_verifier_enable 1

checks.label: Dynamic Code Loading
checks.description: Apps should not use dynamic code loading (security risk)
checks.remediation: Uninstall apps using dynamic code loading: pm uninstall <package>

checks.label: Navigation Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke location access for unneeded nav apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION

checks.label: Device Classification Properties
checks.command: getprop ro.product.device 2>/dev/null; getprop ro.product.model 2>/dev/null; getprop ro.product.manufacturer 2>/dev/null
checks.description: Device identification - document for regulatory purposes
checks.remediation: Record device model and manufacturer for asset inventory and compliance documentation.

checks.label: Root Access (su)
checks.command: su -c 'id' 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'uid=0' && echo 'ROOT_ACTIVE' || which su 2>/dev/null | grep -v '/system/bin/su'
checks.description: Check for actual root shell access (excludes Samsung system su)
checks.remediation: Remove root access by uninstalling su binary or root manager (e.g., pm uninstall com.topjohnwu.magisk).

checks.label: Running Services Count
checks.remediation: Review running services and stop unnecessary ones: am stopservice <component>

checks.label: Xposed Framework
checks.description: Xposed framework enables deep system tweaks
checks.remediation: Uninstall Xposed framework and modules: pm uninstall de.robv.android.xposed.installer

checks.label: Unapproved APKs in /data/local/tmp
checks.remediation: Delete unapproved APKs: rm /data/local/tmp/*.apk

checks.label: Running Services List
checks.command: ps -A 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'ps|grep' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq | head -30
checks.description: All running processes - review for unnecessary services
checks.remediation: Kill unnecessary processes: kill <pid>. Disable unwanted services from auto-starting.

checks.label: Web Server Process
checks.description: Web server running - potential attack surface
checks.remediation: Stop and disable the web server if not required: kill <pid>. Remove the binary if unnecessary.

checks.label: Telnet Daemon
checks.remediation: Kill telnet daemon immediately: kill <pid>. Replace with SSH for remote access.

checks.label: FTP Daemon
checks.description: FTP daemon running - credentials in plaintext!
checks.remediation: Kill FTP daemon immediately: kill <pid>. Replace with SFTP or SCP for secure file transfer.

checks.label: SSH Daemon
checks.remediation: Ensure SSH uses key-based auth and disable password login. Restrict access with AllowUsers directive.

checks.label: MQTT Client/Broker
checks.remediation: Ensure MQTT uses TLS and authentication. Disable anonymous access in broker config.

checks.label: Node.js/Python Services
checks.remediation: Audit script-based services for known vulnerabilities. Update runtimes to latest patched versions.

checks.label: Database Services
checks.remediation: Ensure databases require authentication and are not exposed on public interfaces. Bind to localhost only.

checks.label: Docker/Container Runtime
checks.remediation: Audit running containers for outdated images. Restrict Docker socket access to authorized users only.

checks.label: Init System Type
checks.remediation: Document the init system type. Review startup services for unnecessary or insecure daemons.

checks.label: Custom IoT Daemons
checks.remediation: Audit each custom daemon for necessity and security. Disable unneeded ones via init scripts.

checks.label: Camera Permission Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke camera from untrusted apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.CAMERA

checks.label: Microphone Permission Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke microphone from untrusted apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO

checks.label: Location Permission Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke location from untrusted apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION

checks.label: SMS Permission Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke SMS permission from non-essential apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.SEND_SMS

checks.label: Contacts Permission Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke contacts access from untrusted apps: pm revoke <package> android.permission.READ_CONTACTS

checks.label: Unknown Sources Disabled
checks.description: Installing from unknown sources should be disabled
checks.remediation: Disable unknown sources: settings put secure install_non_market_apps 0

checks.label: Play Protect Enabled
checks.remediation: Enable Play Protect: settings put global package_verifier_user_consent 1

checks.label: Install via ADB Blocked
checks.remediation: Block ADB installs: settings put global install_allow_adb 0

checks.label: Permission Controller Version
checks.command: dumpsys package com.google.android.permissioncontroller 2>/dev/null | grep versionName | head -1
checks.remediation: Update the permission controller via Play Store to ensure latest security patches are applied.

checks.label: Auto Revoke Unused Permissions
checks.remediation: Enable auto-revoke: settings put global auto_revoke_permissions_mode 2

checks.label: Background Location Apps
checks.remediation: Revoke background location: appops set <package> android:coarse_location deny

checks.label: Camera Apps Running
checks.remediation: Force-stop apps using the camera unexpectedly: am force-stop <package>

checks.label: Overlay Permission (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW)
checks.command: DUMP=$(dumpsys package 2>/dev/null); for pkg in $(pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2 | head -30); do echo "$DUMP" | grep -A200 "Package.*$pkg" | head -200 | grep -q 'SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW.*granted=true' && echo "OVERLAY: $pkg"; done
checks.description: Third-party apps with draw-over-other-apps permission - enables phishing overlay attacks on POS/banking screens
checks.remediation: Revoke overlay permission: appops set <package> SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW deny

checks.label: Current Foreground Window
checks.description: Currently focused window and app - useful for detecting active overlay attacks in real-time
checks.remediation: If an unexpected app is in the foreground, force-stop it: am force-stop <package>

checks.label: Backup-Enabled Apps (allowBackup)
checks.command: for pkg in $(pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f2 | head -20); do dumpsys package $pkg 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'allowBackup=true' && echo "BACKUP_ON: $pkg"; done
checks.description: Third-party apps with allowBackup=true - ADB backup can extract app data including credentials and tokens
checks.remediation: Disable ADB backup globally: settings put secure backup_enabled 0. Contact app developers to set allowBackup=false.

checks.label: Frida Detected
checks.remediation: Uninstall Frida: pm uninstall <frida-package>. Remove frida-server binary from /data/local/tmp.

checks.label: Magisk Detected
checks.remediation: Uninstall Magisk: pm uninstall com.topjohnwu.magisk. Reflash stock boot image to fully remove root.

checks.label: Third-party Shared UID Packages
checks.description: Non-system apps sharing UIDs may indicate privilege escalation risk. Apps sharing a UID run in the same process sandbox and can access each other's data.
checks.remediation: Uninstall apps sharing UIDs unless they are from the same trusted vendor: pm uninstall <package>

checks.label: System Apps Signed with v1-only Signature Scheme
checks.command: for pkg in $(pm list packages -s 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^package://' | head -50); do info=$(dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'signatures=|signingInfo' | head -1); echo "$pkg: $info"; done | grep -i 'v1' | head -10
checks.description: System apps signed only with the JAR (v1) signature scheme are vulnerable to Janus-style (CVE-2017-13156) tampering. Modern apps should use signature scheme v2 or v3 (or v4 with incremental). Empty output means no v1-only system apps were found in the sampled set.
checks.remediation: Ensure all system apps are signed with APK signature scheme v2 or v3. Rebuild or re-sign affected apps using apksigner with --v2-signing-enabled and --v3-signing-enabled.

checks.label: Apps Requesting QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES
checks.command: pm list packages -U 2>/dev/null | head -1 >/dev/null; for pkg in $(pm list packages 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^package://' | head -200); do dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES' && echo "$pkg"; done | head -20
checks.description: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES (Android 11+) lets an app enumerate every installed package on the device, bypassing the new package-visibility restrictions. Legitimate uses are narrow (launchers, antivirus). Many sideloaded or adware apps abuse it.
checks.remediation: Review each listed app. Uninstall or revoke the permission for any app whose legitimate function does not require enumerating all installed packages.

checks.label: Apps Requesting REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES
checks.command: for pkg in $(pm list packages 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^package://' | head -200); do dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES' && echo "$pkg"; done | head -20
checks.description: REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES lets an app prompt the user to sideload APKs. Necessary for app stores, browsers, and file managers; abused by malware to drop payloads. On a locked-down kiosk or POS device the list should ideally be empty or limited to the OEM updater.
checks.remediation: Review each listed app. On kiosk/POS devices, restrict this permission to the OEM update agent only; revoke it for browsers, file managers, and unknown apps.
